facts.text: On this date in 1512, the Sistine Chapel ceiling was unveiled to the public — Michelangelo had painted it lying on his back in under four years, a feat so grueling it permanently damaged his eyesight.

On this date in 1993, the Maastricht Treaty took effect, formally creating the European Union and transforming what had been a trade bloc of 12 nations into a political entity of nearly 350 million people.
More people live inside a circle drawn around Dhaka, Bangladesh than in the entire United States west of the Mississippi River.
The country with the world's highest median age is not Japan — it is Monaco, where the median resident is over 55 years old, largely because the wealthy retire there but few children are born.
Istanbul is the only city on Earth that sits on two continents, but it is also the only city whose metropolitan population — 16 million — exceeds that of 130 sovereign nations.
On Nov 1, 1993, the Maastricht Treaty took effect, creating the European Union and setting in motion the euro — a currency that now serves 350 million people who never voted for it directly.
On Nov 1, 1999, Charles Schwab's market cap briefly surpassed Merrill Lynch's — a discount broker worth more than Wall Street's most storied firm, at the peak of the day-trading mania.
The S&P 500 has historically risen in November more than any other month, averaging gains in roughly 75% of all Novembers since 1950.
Berkshire Hathaway's Class A shares have never been split. One share costs over $600,000 — Buffett's deliberate way of filtering out short-term traders.
The Dutch East India Company, history's first publicly traded corporation, paid dividends for nearly 200 consecutive years — funded partly by spice monopolies enforced at gunpoint.
On this day in 1952, the first hydrogen bomb was detonated at Enewetak Atoll — releasing more energy in seconds than all explosives used in World War II combined.
On November 1, 1977, Chiron was discovered: the first known centaur object, orbiting between Saturn and Uranus, blurring the line between asteroid and comet.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
Your body replaces about 3.8 million cells every second — meaning the version of you reading this is, in measurable ways, not the same one who woke up this morning.
Light takes 8 minutes to reach Earth from the Sun, but up to 100,000 years to travel from the Sun's core to its surface, fighting its way through dense plasma.
On this day in 1512, the Sistine Chapel ceiling was unveiled to the public. The United States wouldn't exist for another 264 years.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded.
On this day in 1955, the Vietnam War began by U.S. military reckoning — the same year Disneyland opened and Jonas Salk's polio vaccine was declared safe.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid.
On this day in 1604, Othello received its first recorded performance at the court of King James I. Shakespeare was 40, and had roughly 12 years left to live.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, 2012. Too precise to stay obscure for long.
Hiraeth (n.): a Welsh longing for a home that may never have existed — grief, nostalgia, and yearning fused into one untranslatable ache. English has no equivalent and never will.

On this day in 1512, the Sistine Chapel ceiling was unveiled. The Italian word 'volta' — meaning both 'vault' and 'time' — is why Michelangelo's ceiling and a clock face share the same linguistic root.

Mamihlapinatapai: a Yaghan word from Tierra del Fuego meaning the wordless look shared between two people who both want something neither will initiate. Guinness once called it the most succinct word in existence.

On this day in 1604, Othello was first performed at Whitehall. Shakespeare coined 'bedroom' — used in that play — replacing the older 'bedchamber'. He invented roughly 1,700 words English still uses daily.
On this date in 2008, Satoshi Nakamoto published the Bitcoin whitepaper to a cryptography mailing list. Nine people received it. None responded with enthusiasm.

On Nov 1, 2020, Ethereum's Medalla testnet had already suffered a mass slashing event—over 70,000 validators penalized due to a client bug in Prysm, exposing single-client dependency risk before mainnet.

Bitcoin's script language was intentionally crippled. Satoshi disabled opcodes like OP_MUL and OP_CAT in 2010, fearing attack surface—decisions that still constrain what base-layer Bitcoin can compute today.

The DAO hack of 2016 didn't steal funds instantly. The attacker was locked in a 28-day withdrawal delay by the DAO's own rules, giving Ethereum developers the window to execute a contentious hard fork.
Solana's clock drifts from real time. Its on-chain timestamp is derived from a proof-of-history counter that can diverge from UTC by hours, meaning on-chain 'time' on Solana is formally approximate.

Today in history: On November 1, 2017, Google Brain published 'Attention Is All You Need' — the Transformer paper that eliminated recurrence from sequence models and became the architectural foundation for virtually every major language model since.

Today in history: On November 1, 2022, Stability AI released Stable Diffusion publicly. Within weeks, a single consumer GPU could generate photorealistic images from text — a capability that had required a research lab six months prior.

AlphaFold2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins — essentially the entire known protein universe — in under a year. The task had been biology's central unsolved problem for half a century.

GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed around 50 petaflop/s-days of compute. Training the original 1989 LeNet took roughly 10 flop/s-days. That gap of 13 orders of magnitude happened in 35 years.

RLHF — the technique that makes language models follow instructions — was originally developed for video game agents in 2017. Its application to text generation was not the obvious use case at the time.
